guided_chapters.title: Meet the sarcomere
guided_chapters.learning_objective: Define a sarcomere and distinguish ATP-powered actomyosin contraction from titin's passive spring-and-scaffold roles.
guided_chapters.lay_summary: A sarcomere is the repeating contractile unit between two Z-discs. Adenosine triphosphate (ATP)-powered myosin pulls on actin to drive active contraction; titin is the long passive spring and scaffold that helps the unit recoil and stay organized, not the motor.
guided_chapters.narration: A sarcomere is the repeating contractile unit between two Z-discs. Adenosine triphosphate (ATP)-powered myosin pulls on actin to drive active contraction; titin is the long passive spring and scaffold that helps the unit recoil and stay organized, not the motor.
guided_chapters.state_change_announcement: Showing the full sarcomere and one representative titin route; your current sarcomere length is preserved.
guided_chapters.expected_learner_takeaway: Myosin and actin power active contraction; titin is a passive spring and scaffold spanning the sarcomere.
guided_chapters.expert_expansion: The continuous axial topology and domain order are constrained, while the smooth three-dimensional backbone path remains a schematic presentation of unresolved transverse placement.
not_claimed: known transverse azimuth along the entire chain

guided_chapters.title: Follow one giant molecule
guided_chapters.learning_objective: Trace one representative titin from Z-disc to M-line and distinguish its elastic I-band from its thick-filament-associated A-band.
guided_chapters.lay_summary: Follow one representative titin from its N-terminal end at the Z-disc to its C-terminal end at the central M-line. Its I-band portion is the elastic span that extends, while its A-band portion stays associated with the myosin thick filament.
guided_chapters.narration: Follow one representative titin from its N-terminal end at the Z-disc to its C-terminal end at the central M-line. Its I-band portion is the elastic span that extends, while its A-band portion stays associated with the myosin thick filament.
guided_chapters.state_change_announcement: Framing the full titin route from Z-disc to M-line; your current sarcomere length is preserved.
guided_chapters.expected_learner_takeaway: A single titin path links the Z-disc and M-line, with an elastic I-band portion in series with a bound A-band portion.
guided_chapters.expert_expansion: Domain identity and order follow Q8WZ42; instanced archetypes encode class, position, and orientation rather than unique molecular surfaces. The smooth linkers between them are presentation proxies for unresolved conformations.

guided_chapters.title: See its molecular architecture
guided_chapters.learning_objective: Introduce titin's folded Ig and Fn3 domains and disordered N2A/PEVK elements without moving Fn3 into the elastic I-band.
guided_chapters.lay_summary: Zoom in on titin’s building blocks: folded immunoglobulin-like (Ig) domains, fibronectin type III (Fn3) domains, N2A, and the disordered PEVK spring. The A-band carries the Ig/Fn3 array; this model does not place Fn3 in the elastic I-band.

guided_chapters.title: Stretch the spring
guided_chapters.learning_objective: Compare I-band lengthening with the approximately fixed A-band and distinguish added length, incremental compliance, and modeled passive force.
guided_chapters.lay_summary: As the sarcomere stretches within the supported range, titin’s I-band lengthens while its A-band span stays approximately fixed. The model predicts rising passive force; PEVK takes a growing share of added length and incremental compliance—how readily the next small stretch occurs—not simply more total extension.
guided_chapters.narration: As the sarcomere stretches within the supported range, titin’s I-band lengthens while its A-band span stays approximately fixed. The model predicts rising passive force; PEVK takes a growing share of added length and incremental compliance—how readily the next small stretch occurs—not simply more total extension.
guided_chapters.state_change_announcement: Preparing the stretch comparison without changing your current length. If that length is outside the supported range, Set demonstration start saves it for Restore.
guided_chapters.expected_learner_takeaway: Stretch is concentrated in elastic I-band elements; the A-band stays approximately fixed and modeled passive force rises within the supported range.
guided_chapters.expert_expansion: Regional nanometer partitions and passive force are modeled by a common-force series-chain solver using source-bounded force-extension laws. Incremental compliance is the local change in extension per added force; it is distinct from a segment's absolute length or total extension.

guided_chapters.title: Inspect both anchors
guided_chapters.learning_objective: Explain the Z-disc interaction network without treating telethonin as the sole force path, and identify the source-limited M-line integration network.
guided_chapters.lay_summary: At the Z-disc, titin joins a network containing the actin-crosslinker α-actinin; telethonin binds two antiparallel Z1Z2 fragments but is not the sole force path. At the central M-line, titin meets a protein-crosslinking network whose exact in-situ route remains unresolved.
guided_chapters.narration: At the Z-disc, titin joins a network containing the actin-crosslinker α-actinin; telethonin binds two antiparallel Z1Z2 fragments but is not the sole force path. At the central M-line, titin meets a protein-crosslinking network whose exact in-situ route remains unresolved.
guided_chapters.state_change_announcement: Moving to the Z-disc anchor close-up while retaining the full-sarcomere relationship; your current sarcomere length is preserved.
guided_chapters.expected_learner_takeaway: Both titin ends participate in protein networks; telethonin is one supported Z-disc interaction, not the complete force-transmission route.
guided_chapters.expert_expansion: The antiparallel two-titin-to-one-telethonin topology is structure-supported, but the full in-situ force path remains unresolved. At the other end, titin's C-terminus integrates into a heterogeneous M-band network; sparse schematic relationships avoid inventing exact crosslink identities or coordinates.
not_claimed: telethonin as the sole path carrying titin tension

guided_chapters.lay_summary: Along the A-band, titin associates with the myosin thick filament as a scaffold. The surrounding lattice shows thick and thin filament packing. One representative molecule is shown; copy number, azimuth, and disputed repeat-to-myosin register are not encoded.

expert_cards.title: Spring and scaffold: what the A-band super-repeat does and does not settle
expert_cards.body: The A-band segment contains an eleven-domain C-zone sequence pattern. A fixed rabbit-psoas antibody-localization dataset reports a 3.98 nm mean titin-domain spacing, so this visualization may derive a labelled 43.78 nm display interval for eleven domains. That number is not the approximately 45.54 nm thick-filament L periodicity and does not establish an exact titin–myosin register. The schematic A-band allocation stays constant while sarcomere length changes, so the same molecule reads as an extensible I-band spring in series with an anchored display scaffold. Molecular-ruler and regulatory roles remain active proposals: the visualization encodes no causal mechanism, length-setting rule, or activation coupling.
not_claimed: a settled ruler mechanism for thick-filament length
a settled regulatory pathway from titin to myosin
identity or exact register among the derived 43.78 nm display interval, H periodicity, and L periodicity
an exact universal A-band azimuth for the bound segment

findings.text: The C-zone contains an eleven-domain sequence pattern; this display uses a labelled 43.78 nm interval derived from one source-context mean spacing, not an exact molecular repeat length.
In this model the bound segment's end-to-end span stays constant while sarcomere length changes.
That titin acts as a molecular ruler setting thick-filament length.
That titin participates causally in myosin regulation.

expert_cards.title: Optional MyBP-C context, and why cardiac coordinates were not imported
expert_cards.body: MyBP-C is an accessory C-zone protein of the thick filament, not part of titin. Fast skeletal muscle evidence supports its presence in the C-zone at the approximately 43 nm repeat, with roughly three molecules per repeat, so the optional layer draws that many sparse markers and nothing more. High-resolution coordinates for MyBP-C exist, but they come from cardiac thick-filament reconstructions. The sequence construct and tissue-review status are supplied by the scientific-scope ledger, so adopting a cardiac accessory protein's placement would silently mix preparations. The stripe register, azimuth, reach, and pose therefore stay SCHEMATIC, no molecule is drawn reaching a thin filament, and no titin contact is depicted.
not_claimed: cardiac cMyBP-C coordinates transferred into the reference-sequence model
three exact molecules at every human titin super-repeat
a resolved stripe register, azimuth, reach, or binding pose

findings.text: Fast skeletal MyBP-C occupies the C-zone at the approximately 43 nm thick-filament repeat, at roughly three molecules per repeat.
The stripe register, azimuth, outward reach, and binding pose for this reference-sequence render are unresolved, so the drawn path stays schematic.
Whether a direct titin–MyBP-C contact exists in this scope; none is depicted.

expert_cards.title: N2A as a mechanical and interaction hub
expert_cards.body: The N2A element is more than a length of spring. It contains a structured UN2A core with flexible flanks, and it binds CARP, which makes it a plausible meeting point between mechanical state and signalling. The visualization keeps N2A as a region of titin and adds no partner molecules: naming a binding event is not the same as resolving where the partner sits in an intact sarcomere.

findings.text: N2A contains a structured UN2A core with flexible flanking sequence.
CARP binding to N2A is experimentally characterised.
That N2A acts as an in-situ signalling hub coupling strain to downstream pathways.
The complete composition and geometry of any N2A signalosome in an intact sarcomere.

not_claimed: an added partner molecule in the 3-D scene

expert_cards.title: Titin kinase: an established domain, an unsettled mechanism
expert_cards.body: Titin carries a kinase domain near the A-band/M-band junction. Its presence and its isolated structure are established, and the domain proxy you can see is measured from deposited coordinates. What is not settled is the mechanism: proposals that stretch opens the domain and switches on signalling remain under active debate, so the visualization shows the domain and refuses to animate an activation switch.

findings.text: A kinase domain sits near the A-band/M-band junction of titin.
Isolated kinase-domain structures give the measured proxy dimensions drawn here.
That mechanical strain opens the domain and triggers a specific signalling cascade.
The domain's orientation and conformation inside an intact sarcomere.

expert_cards.title: Length-dependent activation: a proposal, not a simulation
expert_cards.body: Muscle produces more force at longer lengths for a given calcium level, and passive titin tension and MyBP-C are among the contributors proposed to explain it. That is a live hypothesis about how a passive spring might bias myosin's regulatory state. This model does not implement it: sarcomere length and biochemical activation remain independent axes here, and no state variable couples one to the other.

findings.text: Force at a given calcium level depends on sarcomere length.
That passive titin tension contributes causally to that length dependence.
That MyBP-C mediates part of the same thick-filament regulation.
Whether this model could distinguish those proposals; it contains no activation solver.

not_claimed: that titin is the actomyosin motor
automatic coupling between sarcomere length and activation

expert_cards.title: One gene, many titins — and one of them is modelled here
expert_cards.body: A single TTN gene produces many titin isoforms through alternative splicing, and different muscles and tissues express different ones. Isoform choice changes the length and composition of the elastic I-band segment, and therefore passive stiffness. This visualization uses the reference sequence named by the scientific-scope ledger and deliberately adds no second isoform: naming the reference is what keeps a general titin story from becoming a claim about an isoform-neutral molecule.

findings.text: Alternative splicing of one TTN gene yields tissue- and muscle-specific titin isoforms.
The model identity is the reference sequence supplied by the scientific-scope ledger.
How the geometry shown here would differ for another isoform; no second isoform is modelled.

not_claimed: a per-isoform comparison of passive stiffness

expert_cards.title: What this model still cannot tell you
expert_cards.body: Three gaps are worth naming plainly. The azimuthal arrangement of titin strands around a thick filament is resolved in cardiac muscle but not adopted here because that coordinate transfer is outside the admitted structural context. M-band organization is only partly resolved, so the centre is a coordinate reference with sparse schematic crosslinks rather than a structure. And active mechanics are absent entirely: the lattice comparison is a quasi-static length sweep, not a time-resolved contraction.

findings.text: The azimuthal placement of titin strands on a skeletal thick filament; the cardiac arrangement is measured but out of scope.
The molecular organization of the M-band; no M1 density is inferred from the retained averaged maps.
Time-resolved active mechanics, including the real time-varying Poisson ratio of the lattice.

not_claimed: that these gaps are the only ones
